name: The Heritage Oak of Grant Hall

location.address: Academic Mall near Grant Hall, UNLV campus, 4505 S Maryland Pkwy, Las Vegas, NV 89154

access: Free. Public university campus, open grounds, walkable any time the campus is open.
transport: On the UNLV campus; nearest RTC bus stops serve Maryland Parkway, short walk in.
verify_notes: Nevada Big Tree Register (2015) lists 'Heritage Live' Quercus virginiana as a state champion at Clark, University of Nevada, Las Vegas: circumference 46in, height 56ft, spread 41ft, crown pts 10, total 112. UNLV's own Nov 4 2025 news article 'Rooted in Champions' (unlv.edu/news/article/rooted-champions, by Ren McMullin & Becca Schwartz) independently confirms this tree is CURRENTLY a state champion, describes it as a hybrid of English oak height and Bur oak width, ~60 feet tall, on the Academic Mall near Grant Hall, providing summer shade. Small height discrepancy (56ft in 2015 vs ~60ft described in 2025) is consistent with a decade of growth, not a conflict. No exact coordinates in either source; pin is the OSM/Nominatim position of Grant Hall itself, not the tree, so approximate. Age not given by either source and not derivable from girth alone without a published growth rate for this Quercus virginiana x macrocarpa hybrid; leave age empty and let the page ask.

name: The Coolibah Eucalyptus of Winchester Park

location.address: Winchester Park (Winchester Dondero Cultural Center), Las Vegas, NV 89121

access: Free. Clark County-run public park, open during park hours.
transport: Winchester Park, near Desert Inn Road and McLeod Drive, central Las Vegas valley; RTC bus routes serve Desert Inn Road.
verify_notes: Nevada Big Tree Register (2015): Coolibah Eucalyptus, Eucalyptus microtheca, Clark, Las Vegas, Winchester Park, circumference 80in, height 70ft, spread 47ft, total 162pts. The Las Vegas Review-Journal's 2016 piece on the Nevada Big Tree Register independently confirms 'three more champions grow at the Winchester Cultural Center, a county-run park near Desert Inn Road and McLeod Drive', which corroborates the GROUP of three champions at this park (matching the register's three Winchester entries by count and location) but does not name this species individually, so the second source is weaker than a per-species confirmation. No source newer than 2016 found this pass confirming this specific tree; Las Vegas saw a significant windstorm in July 2025 that uprooted many mature trees valley-wide and an ongoing tree-death problem reported locally in 2025 (Fox5 Vegas, Sept 2025), which makes alive-now a real open question here rather than a formality. Flagged for that reason; not known to be dead. Park-level pin (Winchester Park centroid), not the tree itself, hence approximate.
